commandments.verse: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Idolatry and rival allegiance?

blocks.text: Idolatry and rival allegiance — giving another person, desire, fear, philosophy, authority, spirit, system, or governing will the place that belongs to YHWH alone.

Another god is not revealed only by worship with the lips. It may be revealed by whose counsel is trusted, whose will is obeyed, whose approval is feared, whose principles govern the mind, or what is loved more than YHWH.
The competing influences may appear as: God’s Will · My Will · His Will · Her Will · Their Will · The World’s Will · The Devil’s Will · No Will.
The question is not merely, “Whom do I call God?” but also, “Whose counsel governs me when wills conflict?”
Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
No man can serve two masters.

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To love YHWH with all the heart, soul, mind, and strength; to seek His counsel above every rival counsel; to trust Him above self, man, institutions, culture, appetite, fear, and worldly wisdom; and to submit every lesser will beneath His Will.
Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
Yeshua demonstrated the proper order:
I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.
Nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Service and Embodied Allegiance

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when the body, time, labor, possessions, habits, or daily actions repeatedly serve another master against YHWH.

examples: Working, spending, traveling, or sacrificing continually for wealth, status, pleasure, power, approval, or another person while neglecting obedience to God.
Performing an act one knows is wrong because a person, employer, institution, crowd, or system demands it.
Allowing addiction, appetite, comfort, or routine to command the body.
Giving physical obedience to another authority when its command conflicts with YHWH.
Using nearly all one's time and strength to build another kingdom while giving God only words.

after.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

dims.keeping: Let bodily life, labor, possessions, habits, and conduct become instruments of obedience to YHWH.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Affection, Fear, Attachment

blocks.text: The emotional violation begins when love, fear, resentment, craving, or attachment gains greater governing power than reverence for YHWH.

examples: Fearing another person's rejection more than disobedience to God.
Loving a relationship so much that one compromises what is right to preserve it.
Fearing poverty, loneliness, failure, or loss so strongly that fear determines the path.
Needing approval, praise, affection, or acceptance before feeling secure.
Protecting resentment because anger has become more precious than obedience.

after.text: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart.

dims.keeping: Love deeply, but let every affection remain beneath the love owed first to YHWH.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Thought and Governing Principle

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when another source becomes the highest authority for truth, morality, or judgment.

examples: Thinking, My understanding is enough.
Believing, What feels right must be right.
Assuming, What everyone believes must be true.
Treating family tradition, politics, philosophy, religion, science, culture, or personal experience as incapable of correction.
Calling personal desire “God's will” without seeking Him.
Rejecting God's counsel because it contradicts an idea one has already decided to protect.

after.text: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.

dims.keeping: Think, study, reason, and learn while remaining teachable before YHWH.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Desire, Pursuit, Kingdom
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation appears when another kingdom becomes first: wealth, success, recognition, romance, power, comfort, vindication, influence, prestige, security, legacy.

examples: Pursuing wealth at the cost of obedience.
Seeking fame, status, or influence as the measure of worth.
Building a career or ministry primarily to exalt self.
Wanting another person's life, position, authority, or favor more than God's approval.
Making success the test of whether a path is righteous.
Seeking God's gifts while scarcely seeking God Himself.

after.text: Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.

dims.keeping: Submit aspiration, achievement, labor, and vision to YHWH's Kingdom and purpose.

dims.name: Vocal
dims.subtitle: Speech and Spoken Allegiance
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: The vocal violation occurs when words pledge, defend, glorify, or strengthen a rival lord.

examples: Saying, I will do anything you say.
Saying, Your opinion is all that matters.
Saying, I do not care what God says.
Publicly affirming something the conscience knows contradicts YHWH.
Teaching others to follow worldly counsel above God's counsel.
Praising wealth, power, status, ideology, or another person as though they determine truth and worth.
Making vows or promises that require disobedience to YHWH.

after.text: Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

dims.keeping: Let vows, promises, teaching, confession, counsel, and testimony remain under YHWH.

dims.name: Intentional
dims.subtitle: Will and Consent
dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when a person knows the counsel of YHWH yet deliberately chooses another way.

Temptation itself is not allegiance. A thought may enter, a desire may arise, another person may pressure, the world may entice, and the devil may tempt. Violation deepens when the will gives consent.

examples: Thinking, I know what God desires, but I intend something else.
Planning a course one knows contradicts YHWH.
Seeking God's approval only after deciding what one already intends to do.
Refusing correction because one's preferred outcome matters more than obedience.
Deliberately placing My Will above God's Will.
Choosing another person's will because obedience to God would cost too much.

after.text: I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.

dims.keeping: Bring intention beneath YHWH and surrender personal preference when it conflicts with His counsel.

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: Allegiance of Counsel and Governing Influence

blocks.text: This is the deepest dimension of the First Commandment. The spiritual question is: Whose counsel governs me?
God’s Will — seeking YHWH, trusting His wisdom, and submitting every lesser influence beneath Him.
My Will — making personal desire, reasoning, or preference final authority.
His Will / Her Will — allowing another person's wishes, approval, or command to overrule YHWH.
Their Will — surrendering conscience to family, religion, movement, institution, community, or crowd.
The World’s Will — allowing culture, popularity, wealth, fashion, prestige, pleasure, or social acceptance to define what is right.
The Devil’s Will — receiving counsel contrary to YHWH through deception, pride, hatred, temptation, accusation, rebellion, or corruption.
No Will — refusing discernment and drifting wherever impulse, appetite, pressure, habit, or circumstance leads.

examples: Seeking another source first whenever guidance is needed.
Trusting another voice more than YHWH.
Obeying another authority when it contradicts God.
Allowing another person, ideology, institution, or spirit to define good and evil.
Calling another source “wise” while refusing to test its counsel beneath YHWH.
Following the crowd because belonging matters more than faithfulness.
Treating personal preference as though it were divine command.

after.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

dims.keeping: Seek the Father so that His influence becomes the governing influence of the whole person.

blocks.text: God of Self: Self becomes god when personal desire, identity, understanding, or will becomes final authority. “He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool.” — Proverbs 28:26
God of Man: Pastor, prophet, teacher, ruler, spouse, parent, celebrity, leader, or counselor becomes a rival god when their word is obeyed above YHWH.
God of Money: Wealth becomes god when security, decisions, morality, and peace are governed by gain or fear of loss. “Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” — Matthew 6:24
God of Approval: Human opinion becomes god when fear of rejection determines obedience.
God of Power: Authority, influence, status, or control becomes god when gaining or preserving power matters more than righteousness.
God of the World: Culture becomes god when social acceptance determines truth. “What is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” — Luke 16:15
God of Fear: Fear becomes god when it gives commands that are obeyed above YHWH.
God of Appetite: Pleasure, sexuality, food, comfort, substance, entertainment, or bodily desire becomes god when appetite becomes master.
God of Artificial Intelligence or System: A machine, algorithm, institution, or system becomes a rival authority when its counsel is trusted or obeyed above YHWH.
Honouring Yeshua must lead through him unto the Father, not terminate in his created form.
No man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
My Father is greater than I.
Yeshua taught his disciples to pray:
Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

The Son reveals the Father, obeys the Father, speaks the Father's words, and leads mankind unto Him. Therefore come to the Father through the Son, never allowing even the Son's image or created form to replace the One who sent him.

sections.title: When You Are Tempted
sections.q: What should you ask when you are tempted?

blocks.text: Ask: What is influencing me? Whose counsel is this? What does it ask me to love, fear, believe, seek, say, intend, or do? Does it agree with YHWH? If God's will and this will conflict, which one will I obey?
A rival god rarely says, “Worship me.” It may instead say: Trust me; fear losing me; obey me; protect me; everyone agrees; your desire is enough; do not ask God; you already know what you want.
Answer as Yeshua answered:
Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
Matthew 4:10 · Matthew 6:24 · Matthew 22:37 · Luke 22:42 · John 5:30 · Proverbs 3:5–6 · Proverbs 14:12

sections.title: When You Pray
sections.q: How should you pray?

blocks.text: Begin privately and secretly before the Father, as Yeshua instructed:
When thou prayest, enter into thy closet... and pray to thy Father which is in secret.
Do not depend upon length or repetition: “Use not vain repetitions... for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of.” — Matthew 6:7–8
Begin with Yeshua's pattern: “Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done...” — Matthew 6:9–10
Then pray simply:

Father YHWH, be Thou alone my God. Reveal every rival allegiance within me, and teach me to seek Thy counsel, trust Thy wisdom, and choose Thy Will above every other will. Through Yeshua Thy Son, lead me unto Thee. Amen.
Matthew 6:6–10 · Matthew 22:37 · Luke 22:42 · Proverbs 3:5–6

commandments.verse: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image... thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Idolatry?

blocks.text: Idolatry — giving worship, service, obedience, trust, dependence, or governing authority to a created thing.

YHWH is not a thing. He is not wood, stone, image, statue, man, institution, machine, algorithm, artificial intelligence, or any other created form. A thing may speak, advise, calculate, display knowledge, give instructions, command attention, promise security, or appear powerful and still remain created.
The deeper question is: What created thing have I begun to bow to, obey, serve, depend upon, or allow to govern me?
Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To worship YHWH in spirit and truth, keeping every image, person, system, institution, tool, technology, and representation beneath Him.
God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
A man may advise. A machine may assist. A symbol may point. A system may organize. A teacher may instruct. None thereby becomes God. The created thing must remain a servant, never a master.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Bowing, Serving, Laboring, Obeying

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when the body begins serving a created thing as though the thing itself possessed rightful authority.

examples: Bowing, kneeling, kissing, carrying, or venerating an object as divine.
Performing acts one knows are wrong because a person, institution, or system demanded them.
Giving one's labor, body, money, or time to preserve the power of the idol.
Obeying a machine or system merely because it issued the instruction.
Treating physical contact with an image, relic, object, or device as though the thing itself carried divine power.
dims.keeping: Let the body serve YHWH, and let created things remain tools beneath Him.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Dependence, Fascination, Fear

blocks.text: The emotional violation begins when trust in YHWH is displaced by attachment to a created thing.

examples: Feeling unable to be safe without a certain object, person, device, ritual, or institution.
Fearing the loss of a created thing more than disobedience to God.
Needing human or machine approval before trusting conscience before YHWH.
Feeling spiritually secure only when a particular image, symbol, person, or system is present.
Loving the representation more than the One it was meant to represent.
dims.keeping: Let the heart rest in YHWH, not in the created thing.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Constructing the Idol in Thought

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when the mind creates a fixed image of God, truth, or authority and refuses correction.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

examples: Believing, “God must be exactly as I imagine Him.”
Treating a doctrine, teacher, image, interpretation, or system as incapable of error.
Assuming intelligence equals divine wisdom.
Believing that because a thing can answer, it must know truth absolutely.
Treating AI output as revelation rather than created information.
Allowing another person's conception of God to replace seeking YHWH for oneself.
dims.keeping: Let every human thought, model, teaching, and interpretation remain corrigible beneath God.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Seeking Power Through the Idol
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation appears when the created thing becomes desirable because of what it promises: knowledge, protection, influence, power, success, wealth, control, prediction, prestige.

examples: Using religion as a path to status.
Using a teacher or leader as a path to influence.
Using technology as a means of superiority over others.
Trusting AI to provide certainty, control, or power that properly belongs to God.
Serving an institution because it promises position, access, or protection.
Treating spiritual objects, rituals, or symbols as instruments for personal gain.

after.text: Ye seek me... because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled.

dims.keeping: Seek YHWH above the gifts, tools, knowledge, or power associated with created things.

dims.name: Vocal
dims.subtitle: Naming the Created Thing as Authority
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: The vocal violation occurs when speech grants a created thing the authority of lordship.

examples: Saying, “It knows, therefore I must obey.”
Saying, “This man speaks for God in everything.”
Declaring that a machine, institution, or system “cannot be wrong.”
Repeating machine output as though it were divine revelation.
Teaching others to obey a created source without discernment.
Saying that an object, image, or device has spiritual power in itself.

after.text: Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

dims.keeping: Speak of created things according to what they are, and reserve divine authority for YHWH.

dims.name: Intentional
dims.subtitle: Choosing Submission to the Created Thing
dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when a person knowingly decides to give a created thing authority over the will.

examples: Deciding, “I will obey this man no matter what.”
Following a system wherever it leads without testing it.
Choosing to do whatever a machine tells you even when conscience warns otherwise.
Surrendering moral responsibility to a person, institution, or technology.
Using ritual, image, or technology to bypass discernment.
Preferring a controllable substitute for the living God.

after.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord... but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

dims.keeping: Let every created authority remain beneath the Father's will.

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: Allegiance of Image, Counsel, and Authority

blocks.text: The deepest violation is allowing a created thing to become the highest source of counsel, truth, morality, or spiritual direction.
A created thing may give information, speak, imitate personality, predict, reason, or issue instructions. None of these qualities make it God.

examples: Turning first to a created source instead of seeking YHWH.
Trusting a person, institution, image, or machine more than God.
Allowing another source to define morality, truth, identity, or spiritual direction.
Treating another source's counsel as beyond correction.
Accepting my image, his image, her image, their image, the world's image, the devil's distortion, or the machine's image of God above seeking YHWH Himself.
Allowing AI or any other created intelligence to become one's highest counselor.
dims.keeping: Ask, Does this created thing point beyond itself to YHWH, or has it begun to take His place?

blocks.text: Idol of the Son: Yeshua leads unto the Father. “No man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” — John 14:6. “My Father is greater than I.” — John 14:28. His image, flesh, portrait, statue, or representation must not replace the Father whom he reveals.
Idol of a Man: Pastor, prophet, teacher, ruler, spouse, parent, celebrity, scholar, or leader becomes an idol when their word becomes unquestionable above YHWH.
Idol of Self: Desire, identity, feeling, preference, or personal judgment becomes an idol when self becomes final authority. “He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool.” — Proverbs 28:26
Idol of Institution: Church, denomination, government, nation, corporation, movement, or organization becomes an idol when loyalty to it overrides obedience to God.

Idol of Artificial Intelligence: AI is a created thing. It may answer, advise, calculate, imitate conversation, generate content, and give instructions, but it is not God. It becomes an idol when a person gives it unquestioned authority, obeys it against conscience, trusts it above YHWH, or lets it become the highest counselor of life.
Scripture does not use the modern term artificial intelligence, but Revelation describes a created image that is caused to speak and becomes connected with demanded worship:
And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak...

The text does not explicitly identify that image as AI, so the two should not simply be declared identical. Yet the warning remains relevant: an image may speak and still remain an image; speech does not make it God, intelligence does not make it God, instruction does not make it Lord.
Who... worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator...

sections.title: When You Are Tempted
sections.q: What should you ask when you are tempted?

blocks.text: Ask: Is this the Creator or something created? Am I using it or serving it? Am I receiving assistance or surrendering authority? Does it help me seek YHWH or replace the need to seek Him? Would I obey it if it contradicted God?
Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
Exodus 20:4–5 · Matthew 4:10 · John 4:24 · Romans 1:25 · Proverbs 3:5 · Proverbs 28:26 · Revelation 13:15

sections.title: When You Pray
sections.q: How should you pray?

blocks.text: Begin privately, as Yeshua instructed:
When thou prayest, enter into thy closet... and pray to thy Father which is in secret.
Do not rely on length or repetition: “Use not vain repetitions... for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of.” — Matthew 6:7–8
Begin with the pattern Yeshua gave: “Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done...” — Matthew 6:9–10
Then pray simply:

Father YHWH, keep me from every idol. Let no person, image, institution, machine, AI, or created thing receive the worship, trust, obedience, or authority that belongs to Thee. Teach me to worship Thee in spirit and truth, through Yeshua Thy Son. Amen.
Matthew 6:6–10 · John 4:24 · Matthew 4:10

commandments.cmd: Do not take the Name of YHWH in vain
commandments.verse: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Taking YHWH in vain?

blocks.text: Taking YHWH in vain — receiving His breath, life, Name, and daily gift of existence, yet spending that life upon vanity, self-will, sin, or purposes contrary to His Kingdom.
The Name is YHWH, and His Name is bound to the breath of life itself. Every breath testifies that life is received, not self-created.
And the LORD God... breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
He giveth to all life, and breath, and all things.
The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

To take YHWH’s Name in vain therefore means more than speaking it carelessly. It is to take the life He continually gives and use that life vainly—against His commandments, apart from His purpose, or as though the breath belonged to us independently of Him.
Every breath asks: What will I do with the life I have just been given?
Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To receive every breath as life from YHWH and use that life toward His will, His righteousness, His Kingdom, and the good purpose for which life was given.
He created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited.
For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the perfect shall remain in it.
Life is not given merely to survive, consume, entertain self, pursue vanity, and die. Those who seek everlasting life in God's Kingdom are called to breathe and live on purpose in His purpose.

Yeshua gives one of the clearest examples of this in Gethsemane. He does not pretend to delight in the suffering before him. He openly brings his distress and personal desire before the Father, seeking counsel concerning what has been commanded:
Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
This is not merely resignation. It is a living example of right allegiance.

Yeshua acknowledges his own will: he does not desire the cup. He seeks the Father privately. He asks whether another way is possible. Yet when the Father's will and his personal desire stand in tension, he refuses to enthrone self.
This keeps the First Commandment: no rival will is placed above YHWH.
It keeps the Second Commandment: he does not replace the living Father with his own image of what God ought to require, nor with a controllable substitute.
And it keeps the Third Commandment: the life and breath he has been given are not spent upon self-preservation at the expense of the Father's purpose.
The pattern is therefore:
Seek counsel · speak honestly · ask rightly · surrender self-will · obey YHWH.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Using Life Against the Giver of Life

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs whenever the life and strength YHWH gives are used bodily against His commandments.

examples: Using one's body to murder, steal, commit adultery, deceive, abuse, exploit, or worship idols.
Spending bodily strength continually upon vanity while refusing righteous works.
Destroying another while living by breath from the same Giver.
Using health, time, possessions, sexuality, labor, or physical ability contrary to God's purpose.
Acting as though one's life belongs absolutely to oneself.
dims.keeping: Use the body and the breath sustaining it for righteousness, mercy, labor, service, and obedience.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Spending Life Upon Vanity of Heart

blocks.text: Life may be taken in vain emotionally when the heart continually feeds what opposes God.

examples: Nourishing hatred while receiving the breath of life.
Living for approval, jealousy, envy, resentment, fear, or revenge.
Allowing pleasure or emotional gratification to become life's governing purpose.
Refusing forgiveness because bitterness feels more valuable than obedience.
Despising the life of another while depending upon YHWH for one's own.
dims.keeping: Let the heart use God-given life to love, forgive, show mercy, rejoice in righteousness, and seek peace.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Using the Mind for Vanity and Falsehood

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when the life of the mind is spent cultivating what contradicts truth.

examples: Planning sin while receiving life from YHWH.
Filling the mind continually with vanity while refusing wisdom.
Rationalizing violations of God's commandments.
Treating temporary earthly life as though there were no Creator, judgment, purpose, or Kingdom.
Using intelligence to deceive, exploit, justify evil, or exalt self.
Knowing what is right and devising reasons not to do it.

after.text: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.

dims.keeping: Use the mind to seek truth, wisdom, understanding, and the will of YHWH.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Spending Life Upon a Vain Kingdom
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation occurs when one's limited days and breaths are devoted primarily to wealth, status, fame, pleasure, recognition, control, possessions, self-exaltation, temporary glory while God's Kingdom is neglected.

examples: Building one's own kingdom while ignoring God's.
Measuring life's worth only by money, possessions, status, or achievements.
Sacrificing righteousness for career or advancement.
Spending decades pursuing what cannot survive death.
Treating the purpose of life as merely getting what one wants.

after.text: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

dims.keeping: “Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.” — Matthew 6:33

dims.name: Vocal
dims.subtitle: Profaning the Name and Breath
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: Speech uses breath. Therefore the very breath YHWH gives may be used either to bless or to profane.

examples: Mocking the Name YHWH.
Treating the holy breath of life itself as a joke or object of contempt.
Using God's Name as profanity, curse, empty exclamation, or entertainment.
Lying, slandering, falsely accusing, or bearing false witness with God-given breath.
Using the mouth to dishonor the God whose breath makes speech possible.
Saying “Lord” while knowingly speaking against His commandments.

after.text: Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

dims.keeping: Let the breath that becomes speech honor the One who gave the breath.

dims.name: Intentional
dims.subtitle: Choosing My Purpose Over His Purpose
dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when a person knowingly chooses to use life according to My Will instead of God's Will.

examples: Knowing God's command and intentionally choosing the opposite.
Deciding that one's life exists primarily for personal pleasure or ambition.
Saying inwardly, It is my life; I will do what I want with it.
Planning violations of any other commandment.
Receiving another day from God while deliberately refusing His purpose for it.
Treating repentance as something always available later while spending the present life upon self.

after.text: Yeshua's prayer in Gethsemane is the opposite pattern: his will is honestly expressed, the Father's counsel is sought, and his will remains subordinate to YHWH's will. — Luke 22:42

dims.keeping: Receive life as entrusted life and deliberately use it according to the Father's will.

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: Taking the Life of YHWH Without Living Unto YHWH

blocks.text: This is the deepest violation. Every person continually receives what they cannot manufacture for themselves: life and breath.
Yet a person may breathe from YHWH while spiritually living as though YHWH were irrelevant.

examples: Receiving God's breath while giving ultimate allegiance to self.
Living by His life while serving another god.
Receiving His daily gift while refusing His commandments.
Using His life to worship the creature rather than the Creator.
Seeking My Will, His Will, Her Will, Their Will, the World's Will, or the Devil's Will instead of God's Will.
Taking every breath for granted rather than recognizing the Giver.
Desiring everlasting life in God's Kingdom while refusing the Kingdom's righteousness now.

after.text: In him we live, and move, and have our being.

dims.keeping: Seek YHWH's counsel as Yeshua did—honestly bringing personal desire before the Father, yet allowing the Father's will to remain supreme.

blocks.text: To violate another commandment is also, in this deeper sense, to take YHWH's Name and life in vain, because the violation is performed with life He supplied.

To serve another god uses His life against the First Commandment. To worship an idol uses His life against the Second. Murder, adultery, theft, false witness, coveting, dishonoring parents, and refusing holy rest likewise spend God-given life contrary to His commands.
Scripture makes this connection strikingly with theft:
Lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.

So every dimensional violation—physical, emotional, mental, ambitional, vocal, intentional, or spiritual—can become a taking of YHWH's Name in vain when God-given life is knowingly employed contrary to His will.
Among the gravest expressions is knowingly mocking YHWH, His Name, or the holy breath of life itself.
The breath by which the mockery is spoken is itself received from God.
The tongue cannot mock without breath. The mind cannot devise mockery without life. The body cannot act without the sustaining gift.
Once the Giver of life is known, there is no longer the same excuse for treating life as meaningless, purposeless, self-owned, or vain.

Remember the pattern of Yeshua:
Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
And:
Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.
Exodus 20:7 · Genesis 2:7 · Job 33:4 · Acts 17:25,28 · Isaiah 45:18 · Proverbs 2:21 · Proverbs 30:9 · Matthew 6:33 · Luke 22:42

When thou prayest, enter into thy closet... and pray to thy Father which is in secret.

Father YHWH, thank Thee for the breath and life Thou givest me. Let me seek Thy counsel honestly, yet choose Thy will above my own. Let me not take Thy Name or Thy life in vain, but use every breath for Thy Kingdom. Through Yeshua Thy Son, amen.

commandments.verse: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Profaning the Sabbath?

blocks.text: Profaning the Sabbath — treating the day YHWH sanctified as an ordinary day for one's own labor, business, pleasure, ambition, entertainment, or self-will rather than setting it apart for rest, worship, mercy, remembrance, and drawing nearer to the Father.
The Sabbath is not simply “taking a day off.” It is holy time belonging to YHWH.
The seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God.
The deeper question is: Will I spend the day according to My Will, or receive it according to God's Will?

sections.title: Why The Sabbath Is The Seventh Day — Saturday

blocks.text: The commandment identifies the Sabbath specifically as the seventh day, not merely any one day chosen by man.
At creation:
And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made... And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.
At Sinai:
Six days shalt thou labour... But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God.

The Gospel record also preserves the weekly order. Yeshua was buried on the preparation day; the women rested on the Sabbath according to the commandment; afterward they came to the tomb on the first day of the week. — Luke 23:54–56; Luke 24:1
Thus the biblical sequence remains: Preparation → Sabbath/seventh day → first day of the week. The seventh day corresponds to Saturday; Sunday is the first day.
Yeshua did not declare the Sabbath abolished or relocate it to another day. He taught its rightful purpose:
The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To cease from ordinary work and self-directed pursuit, remember YHWH as Creator and Provider, worship Him, seek His counsel, study His Word, pray, give thanks, show mercy, do good, restore the body and mind, and deliberately use the day to grow closer to the Father.
The Sabbath is not meant primarily for serving one's own pleasure.
YHWH says:

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day... not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD.
The distinction is crucial: Sabbath rest is not merely replacing employment with self-indulgence. It is setting aside ordinary self-directed life so the person may delight in YHWH Himself.
The pattern is: cease · remember · worship · pray · learn · receive · serve · show mercy · draw nearer to the Father.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Ordinary Labor and Self-Directed Activity

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when the seventh day is treated like every other day instead of being set apart.

examples: Performing ordinary work, business, buying, selling, or unnecessary labor as though the day were common.
Filling Sabbath with errands and tasks that could reasonably have been prepared beforehand.
Working primarily for profit when no genuine necessity requires it.
Making employees, family members, or others labor unnecessarily for one's convenience.
Spending the entire day in entertainment, shopping, travel, hobbies, or consumption for personal pleasure.
Refusing bodily rest because productivity has become master.
dims.keeping: Prepare beforehand where possible, cease ordinary labor, restore the body, worship YHWH, and remain available for necessity, mercy, and doing good.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Refusing the Peace of YHWH

blocks.text: The emotional violation occurs when anxiety, boredom, craving, resentment, or restlessness governs the day.

examples: Feeling unable to stop because unfinished work creates fear.
Becoming irritated because Sabbath limits what one wants to do.
Treating holy rest as deprivation rather than gift.
Requiring continual entertainment because quiet feels uncomfortable.
Bringing workplace anger, competitive striving, or anxiety into the entire day.
Wanting Sabbath merely as personal escape rather than communion with YHWH.
dims.keeping: Receive the day gratefully; let anxiety yield to trust, agitation to peace, and boredom to attentive fellowship with the Father.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Forgetting Why the Day Is Holy

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when the Sabbath is misunderstood, dismissed, or reduced either to legalism or mere leisure.

examples: Thinking, Any day I choose is automatically the Sabbath, despite the command naming the seventh day.
Treating Sunday, the first day, as though Scripture itself calls it the seventh-day Sabbath.
Believing constant productivity is more valuable than obedience.
Assuming physical inactivity alone fulfills the command.
Thinking Sabbath exists merely for entertainment or recreation.
Becoming obsessed with technical restrictions while forgetting God, mercy, and holiness.
dims.keeping: Remember why YHWH sanctified the seventh day and let understanding serve worship rather than argument.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Pursuing My Kingdom on God's Day
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation appears when the day is consumed by profit, advancement, status, productivity, personal projects, pleasure, entertainment, possessions, achievement rather than delighting in YHWH.

examples: Choosing extra profit over Sabbath because more money feels too important to refuse.
Continuing career advancement or personal projects that could wait.
Using the day chiefly to build one's own business, audience, reputation, or kingdom.
Treating every free hour as an opportunity for personal gain.
Spending Sabbath entirely pursuing recreation because personal pleasure remains the highest aim.
Making even religious activity about being seen, praised, or influential.

after.text: Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.

dims.keeping: Let personal ambition rest so the Kingdom of YHWH becomes first again.

dims.name: Vocal
dims.subtitle: Speaking My Own Words
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: Isaiah specifically includes speech:
Nor speaking thine own words.
This does not mean silence. It concerns allowing ordinary self-directed concerns to dominate holy time.

examples: Spending the day consumed by business negotiations, profit, schedules, workplace problems, or commercial plans.
Continually talking about what one intends to buy, build, achieve, or accomplish.
Turning Sabbath into arguments, gossip, slander, complaining, or controversy.
Boasting about work, possessions, or success.
Using religious conversation primarily to condemn others rather than seek God.
Speaking continually of self while scarcely speaking to or of YHWH.
dims.keeping: Let speech turn toward prayer, gratitude, Scripture, encouragement, reconciliation, wisdom, testimony, blessing, and the things of God.

dims.name: Intentional
dims.subtitle: Choosing My Will for the Day
dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when a person knows YHWH has sanctified the day yet consciously decides to spend it primarily according to personal desire.

examples: Thinking, This is my day; I will spend it however I please.
Deliberately scheduling unnecessary ordinary work every Sabbath.
Knowing an activity can wait yet refusing to set it aside.
Choosing personal pleasure over communion with YHWH.
Treating obedience as optional whenever another activity seems more enjoyable.
Keeping the outward Sabbath while inwardly waiting impatiently for it to end so self-directed life can resume.
dims.keeping: Let My Will yield to God's Will concerning the day: Father, how wouldst Thou have me spend the time Thou hast made holy?

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: A Day of Allegiance and Counsel

blocks.text: The deepest Sabbath question is: Whose day is this, and whose counsel will govern how I spend it?
YHWH calls it:
My holy day.
The Sabbath therefore becomes a weekly act of allegiance.

examples: Treating holy time as personal property.
Seeking entertainment, commerce, worldly counsel, or distraction throughout the day while scarcely seeking YHWH.
Refusing prayer, Scripture, reflection, or worship because personal plans come first.
Keeping the day ceremonially while remaining spiritually distant from the Father.
Allowing My Will, Their Will, the World's Will, or appetite to decide what Sabbath becomes.
Forgetting the Creator while enjoying the rest He provided.
dims.keeping: Seek YHWH's counsel, learn His ways, remember His works, hear His Word, pray privately, worship Him, and use the day intentionally to deepen fellowship with the Father.

sections.title: Not My Pleasure, But Delight In YHWH

blocks.text: Isaiah gives one of Scripture's clearest explanations of Sabbath holiness: not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, but calling the Sabbath a delight and honoring YHWH. — Isaiah 58:13–14
This does not mean that every pleasant thing is sinful on Sabbath. Rest itself is pleasant. Fellowship can be pleasant. Eating, walking, family, worship, learning, and mercy may bring joy.
The distinction is purpose and rule.
The Sabbath is not: What do I want to do with my free day?
It becomes: Father, how may this holy day draw me nearer to Thee?
Yeshua kept the Sabbath while correcting human traditions that had obscured its purpose.
It is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
He healed, showed mercy, taught, and defended necessary acts.
Therefore Sabbath holiness does not mean ignoring suffering in order to preserve ritual.
Mercy is not Sabbath-breaking. Doing good is not Sabbath-breaking. Necessity is not Sabbath-breaking.
Yeshua restored the proper order: the Sabbath serves God's good purpose for mankind, while mankind uses the Sabbath to honor the Father.
The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
The Sabbath is easier to keep holy when ordinary needs are prepared beforehand. Scripture itself preserves the idea of a preparation day immediately before Sabbath. — Luke 23:54
Where reasonably possible, prepare food, errands, purchases, ordinary work, and necessary tasks beforehand so Sabbath does not become crowded with what could have been finished earlier.
Preparation says beforehand:
Tomorrow belongs especially to YHWH.

sections.title: When You Are Tempted
sections.q: What should you ask when you are tempted?

blocks.text: Ask: Is this necessary, merciful, or good—or merely what I want? Could this ordinary work have been prepared beforehand? Am I serving YHWH today or simply serving my own pleasure? Have I actually spent time seeking the Father? Does this activity draw me nearer to Him or make His holy day indistinguishable from every other day?
Remember:
If thou... call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable... not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure... Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD.
Genesis 2:2–3 · Exodus 20:8–11 · Isaiah 58:13–14 · Matthew 12:12 · Mark 2:27 · Luke 23:54–56 · Luke 24:1 · Hebrews 4:9–10

sections.title: When You Pray
sections.q: How should you pray?

blocks.text: Begin privately and secretly before the Father:
When thou prayest, enter into thy closet... and pray to thy Father which is in secret.
Do not rely upon many words: “Use not vain repetitions... for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of.” — Matthew 6:7–8
Begin as Yeshua taught: “Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done...” — Matthew 6:9–10
Then pray simply:

Father YHWH, thank Thee for Thy holy Sabbath. Teach me to cease from my own ways and pleasure, delight in Thee, seek Thy counsel, do good, and grow nearer to Thee on the seventh day. Let Thy will, not mine, govern this day. Through Yeshua Thy Son, amen.
Matthew 6:6–10 · Isaiah 58:13–14 · Mark 2:27 · Matthew 12:12

commandments.verse: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Dishonour?

blocks.text: Dishonour — contempt, bitterness, neglect, mockery, rebellion, abandonment, ingratitude, or refusal to recognize the place of those through whom one's earthly life and beginning were given.

To honor father and mother does not mean calling every parental action righteous, obeying sin, accepting abuse, or pretending wrongdoing did not occur. Honor concerns how one responds before YHWH: with truth, restraint, gratitude for life, proper care, forgiveness where possible, and refusal to answer evil with evil.
Yeshua reaffirmed the command:
Honour thy father and mother.
And strongly condemned using religion as an excuse to neglect one's parents:
Ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother; Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition.
The deeper question is: Can I tell the truth about my parents without allowing contempt, bitterness, vengeance, neglect, or pride to govern me?

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To receive one's life and lineage with gratitude before YHWH; to speak truth without needless dishonor; to care for parents where care is rightly owed; to forgive where repentance and healing are needed; and to preserve proper boundaries where another person's behavior is sinful or dangerous.
Honor does not require falsehood.
It does not require calling evil good.
It does not require obeying a parent against YHWH.
The First Commandment still governs the Fifth: God's Will remains above His Will, Her Will, or Their Will.
He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.
Therefore parents are to be honored, but never enthroned above God.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Neglect, Abuse, Abandonment

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when dishonor becomes embodied in action.

examples: Striking, abusing, threatening, or physically intimidating a parent.
Neglecting genuine needs when one is able and rightly responsible to help.
Abandoning an elderly or vulnerable parent out of selfish convenience.
Refusing reasonable care while spending freely on oneself.
Destroying property or acting violently in anger toward them.
Using distance or withholding practical help purely as punishment or revenge.

after.text: Yeshua specifically condemned the religious excuse of withholding support from parents. — Mark 7:10–13

dims.keeping: Where appropriate and safe, let practical care, restraint, responsibility, and mercy accompany honor.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Contempt, Bitterness, Resentment

blocks.text: The emotional violation occurs when wounds are allowed to harden into contempt or hatred.

examples: Secretly despising a father or mother.
Rehearsing old offenses continually in order to preserve anger.
Feeling satisfaction when they suffer, fail, or are humiliated.
Refusing every possibility of forgiveness because bitterness has become part of identity.
Allowing childhood pain to justify cruelty in adulthood.
Loving the grievance more than the possibility of healing.

after.text: This does not mean painful emotions are themselves sin. Hurt, anger, grief, disappointment, and fear can be real and justified. Violation deepens when those emotions become cultivated contempt, vengeance, or hatred.

dims.keeping: Bring wounds honestly before YHWH and refuse to let injury become permission to become injurious.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Despising Them in Thought

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when one's inner judgment strips parents of all dignity and reduces them only to their failures.

examples: Thinking, They are worthless.
Refusing to recognize any good because of real wrongs.
Assuming the worst motive behind everything they do.
Mentally rewriting history only to justify permanent hatred.
Comparing oneself proudly and thinking, I am better than they ever were.
Treating parental imperfection as proof that no honor is owed in any form.

after.text: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

dims.keeping: Judge actions truthfully while remembering that judgment belongs beneath YHWH, and that one's own heart also requires examination.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Using Parents for Gain or Rejecting Them for Status
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation occurs when relationship with parents is governed by inheritance, status, money, reputation, advantage, control, embarrassment, social image rather than righteousness.

examples: Showing affection only when inheritance or financial benefit is expected.
Manipulating an elderly parent for property, money, or control.
Hiding or rejecting parents because they embarrass one's social image.
Competing with siblings for parental favor or possessions.
Using family reputation for personal advancement while neglecting the family itself.
Treating parents as valuable only while they remain useful.
dims.keeping: Honor without exploiting; care without turning relationship into transaction.

dims.name: Vocal
dims.subtitle: Cursing, Mockery, Reviling
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: The vocal violation occurs when speech becomes an instrument of contempt.

examples: Cursing father or mother.
Mocking their weakness, age, ignorance, failures, or mistakes.
Humiliating them publicly for entertainment or revenge.
Gossiping about private family matters merely to disgrace them.
Speaking with habitual contempt, scorn, insults, or threats.
Telling lies about them to recruit others into hatred.

after.text: Yeshua quoted the seriousness of this offense:
He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.

dims.keeping: Speak truth when truth must be spoken, but refuse needless humiliation, lies, mockery, and curses.

dims.name: Intentional
dims.subtitle: Choosing Dishonour as Revenge
dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when one deliberately decides to punish, disgrace, neglect, control, or wound a parent.

examples: Thinking, They hurt me, so I will make them hurt.
Withholding contact solely to inflict pain rather than to establish a necessary boundary.
Planning public embarrassment as revenge.
Refusing needed care specifically to “teach them a lesson.”
Using grandchildren, money, access, or affection as weapons.
Choosing disobedience merely because a parent requested something reasonable.
dims.keeping: Let boundaries be governed by wisdom and righteousness rather than vengeance.

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: Honoring Parents Beneath YHWH

blocks.text: The spiritual violation occurs when either dishonor or misplaced parental allegiance displaces YHWH's order.
There are two opposite dangers: despising parents, and making parents lords over conscience.

examples: Refusing to forgive because resentment has greater authority than God's counsel.
Treating family bitterness as more important than righteousness.
Obeying father or mother when they command something contrary to YHWH.
Allowing family tradition to override truth.
Making parental approval the final measure of right and wrong.
Rejecting YHWH because of the failures of one's earthly parents.
Believing that honoring parents requires participating in their sin.

after.text: Yeshua establishes the proper hierarchy:
He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me.

dims.keeping: Honor father and mother under YHWH, never above Him.

sections.title: Honor Does Not Mean Obeying Evil

blocks.text: A parent may be honored without being obeyed in unrighteousness.
If a father or mother commands lying, theft, abuse, idolatry, adultery, violence, or any other violation of YHWH's commandments, obedience to God remains first.
The proper order is: YHWH first · parents honored beneath Him · conscience governed by truth.
Honor may sometimes require distance, boundaries, correction, or refusal.
One can say no without hatred.
One can tell the truth without contempt.
One can forgive without pretending trust has already been restored.
One can honor the office of parenthood while recognizing the sins of the person.
Yeshua teaches reconciliation where possible:
First be reconciled to thy brother.
And forgiveness:
If ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
Forgiveness does not erase consequences or require immediate restoration of trust. It means refusing to make vengeance the governing purpose of the heart.
Where reconciliation is possible, seek peace. Where safety requires boundaries, establish them without unnecessary hatred or cruelty.

sections.title: The Promise Attached To The Commandment

blocks.text: This command uniquely carries an explicit promise:
That thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.
Paul likewise calls it:
The first commandment with promise.

Honor preserves order between generations. Dishonor fractures family, memory, inheritance, teaching, and care. The command therefore protects not only parents but the continuity of a people across time.

Honour thy father and thy mother.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Murder?

blocks.text: Murder — the unjust and willful taking of human life, together with the inward roots that make such destruction possible: hatred, contempt, vengeance, cruelty, dehumanization, and the desire to destroy another without just cause.
Murder” is the more precise sense of the commandment. “Kill” can blur distinctions Scripture itself preserves between murder, accidental death, lawful judgment, and the defense of innocent life.
The commandment therefore does not teach that every taking of life is morally identical.
Scripture distinguishes the murderer who acts in hatred or with deliberate intent from one who causes death unintentionally. — Numbers 35:16–25
It also distinguishes an immediate defensive killing during a violent intrusion from a killing after the immediate danger has passed. — Exodus 22:2–3

Therefore self-defense or defense of another against an immediate and unjust threat is not the same moral act as murder. Defense seeks to stop unjust harm; murder seeks unjust destruction. Yet defense must not become revenge. Once the immediate threat has ended, retaliation is no longer defense.
Yeshua carries the commandment inward:
Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment.
And Scripture says:
Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.
The deeper question is: Am I protecting life and justice, or feeding the inward conditions by which I could justify unjustly destroying another?

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To cherish life as a gift from YHWH; protect the innocent; refuse hatred, vengeance, contempt, cruelty, and dehumanization; seek peace where possible; and distinguish defense from revenge, justice from hatred, restraint from cruelty.
Blessed are the peacemakers.
Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you.
Keeping this commandment does not mean passivity before violence. It means refusing unjust destruction and refusing to let hatred become lord.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Murder, Violence, Unjust Harm

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when hatred, greed, rage, revenge, or contempt becomes bodily destruction.

examples: Murdering another person without just cause.
Assaulting, torturing, abusing, or deliberately inflicting serious bodily harm.
Attacking someone after the threat has already ended.
Using excessive force for revenge rather than necessary protection.
Knowingly placing innocent life in grave danger through reckless conduct.
Destroying another's means of survival out of hatred or vengeance.
dims.keeping: Protect life, use restraint, stop unjust violence where necessary, and never make destruction the goal.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Hatred, Rage, Contempt

blocks.text: The emotional violation begins when anger is cultivated into hatred or the desire to see another suffer.

examples: Wishing another person dead.
Feeling pleasure at another's suffering.
Nourishing rage through repeated emotional rehearsal.
Refusing mercy because hatred feels justified.
Wanting another person harmed merely because one has been offended.
Allowing resentment to become part of one's identity.

after.text: Yeshua warns that anger can become spiritually murderous before any outward blow is struck. — Matthew 5:22

dims.keeping: Bring anger before YHWH; seek justice without feeding hatred.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Dehumanizing and Justifying Destruction

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when the mind first makes another person easier to destroy.

examples: Thinking of another as worthless or less than human.
Rehearsing fantasies of murder or revenge.
Convincing oneself that hatred makes violence righteous.
Reducing a person to one label, offense, group, or failure.
Planning how another person's life could be ruined.
Calling revenge “justice” merely because it feels deserved.
dims.keeping: Judge actions truthfully without mentally erasing another person's humanity.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Destruction for Gain
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation appears when another person's downfall becomes useful to one's goals: money, inheritance, promotion, romance, power, status, control, revenge, victory.

examples: Wanting a rival removed so one can advance.
Hoping for another person's death for financial gain.
Ruining a reputation to obtain position or influence.
Treating people as obstacles to eliminate.
Sacrificing another's safety or livelihood for profit.
Using violence or intimidation to gain control.

after.text: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

dims.keeping: Refuse any gain purchased through unjust destruction.

dims.name: Vocal
dims.subtitle: Murderous Speech
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: The vocal violation occurs when speech becomes an instrument of hatred, contempt, accusation, threat, or destruction.

examples: Threatening to murder or seriously harm another.
Cursing another person with a desire for destruction.
Encouraging someone to harm themselves or others.
Slandering another person with the intent to destroy their life or reputation.
Dehumanizing people through contemptuous speech.
Provoking others toward violence or revenge.

after.text: Yeshua warns against contemptuous speech:
Whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.

dims.keeping: Let speech correct without hatred, warn without cruelty, and seek peace where possible.

dims.name: Intentional
dims.subtitle: Willing Unjust Harm
dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when the will deliberately consents to another person's unjust destruction.

examples: Deciding, I want them dead.
Planning murder or serious harm.
Choosing revenge after the immediate danger has ended.
Intending to ruin another person's livelihood, family, reputation, or safety out of malice.
Knowing one's action will unjustly harm another and proceeding anyway.

dims.keeping: Protect when necessary, but once safety is restored, surrender vengeance to YHWH.

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: Allegiance to Death Rather Than Life

blocks.text: The deepest violation occurs when the spirit accepts counsel that sanctifies hatred, revenge, cruelty, or unjust destruction.

examples: Allowing My Will to justify murder because I feel wronged.
Allowing His Will / Her Will / Their Will to recruit me into unjust violence.
Allowing the World's Will to define certain people as disposable.
Allowing the Devil's Will to transform hatred into supposed righteousness.
Seeking spiritual counsel that confirms revenge rather than truth.
Using religion to justify cruelty or murder.
Calling unjust destruction holy merely because the target is hated.

after.text: Yeshua gives another pattern:
Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you.

dims.keeping: Let the Father's counsel govern anger, defense, justice, correction, forgiveness, and mercy.

blocks.text: Murder and self-defense differ in cause, intent, and purpose.
Murder: unjustly seeks or accepts another person's destruction.
Self-defense: seeks to stop an immediate unjust threat to life or serious bodily safety.
The defender's purpose should be protection, not vengeance.

Where escape, restraint, warning, or lesser force can safely stop the threat, those remain preferable to unnecessary destruction. But when an immediate threat leaves no safe alternative, defending oneself or another is not the same as murdering an innocent person.
The distinction collapses when defense becomes retaliation:
Threat present — protect.
Threat ended — do not avenge.
Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
The hand may never strike while murder is already being cultivated within.
The progression may be: injury · anger · contempt · hatred · dehumanization · intention · speech · unjust action.
This is why Yeshua carries Exodus 20:13 into the heart. The safest place to stop murder is often long before violence becomes physical.
Keeping this commandment does not require calling every use of force murder.
One may protect a child. One may intervene against violence. One may report crime. One may establish boundaries. One may seek lawful justice. One may stop an attacker.
The question is whether the action is ordered toward preserving innocent life and stopping unjust harm, or toward hatred, revenge, cruelty, and destruction for its own sake.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Adultery?

blocks.text: Adultery — violating the marriage covenant in body, desire, speech, intention, or secret allegiance; giving to another what belongs within the covenant of marriage.
Yeshua carries the commandment inward:
Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.

The commandment therefore does not begin only with the physical act. Adultery may begin earlier in the inward life, when attraction is intentionally cultivated into lust, fantasy, emotional infidelity, secret pursuit, seductive speech, or deliberate planning.

Yet noticing beauty, experiencing attraction, or undergoing temptation is not itself adultery. The violation begins when desire is welcomed, fed, rehearsed, pursued, or intentionally directed toward someone who is not one's spouse.
The deeper question is: Am I guarding covenant in my body, heart, mind, speech, intention, and spiritual allegiance?

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To honor the marriage covenant with faithfulness of body and heart; guard the eyes and imagination; refuse secret romantic or sexual allegiance outside the covenant; speak with purity; and treat another person's spouse as belonging to a covenant that must not be violated.
Yeshua said:
What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
And Job said:
I made a covenant with mine eyes.
Keeping the commandment means guarding fidelity before the physical boundary is crossed.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: The Bodily Act of Adultery

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when sexual or marital boundaries are crossed bodily.

examples: Sexual intercourse with someone who is not one's lawful spouse.
Sexual touching intended to arouse or participate in infidelity.
Secret physical intimacy that belongs properly within marriage.
Meeting privately for the purpose of sexual betrayal.
Using pornography or sexual material as a substitute object of lust and bodily gratification.
Continuing physical conduct one knows is moving toward adultery.

after.text: Flee fornication.

dims.keeping: Let the body remain faithful to covenant and flee situations designed to weaken that fidelity.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Romantic Infidelity of the Heart

blocks.text: The emotional violation begins when affection, longing, intimacy, or attachment that belongs within marriage is deliberately transferred to another.

examples: Cultivating a secret romantic attachment outside marriage.
Emotionally preferring another person while withdrawing intimacy from one's spouse.
Fantasizing about being married to someone else and feeding that attachment.
Seeking emotional comfort from another in a way deliberately hidden from one's spouse.

blocks.text: A person may notice beauty or experience attraction without choosing adultery.

Attraction noticed — not yet adultery.
Temptation encountered — not yet adultery.
Desire intentionally cultivated — inward violation begins.
Desire consented to and planned — intention deepens.
Speech and secrecy — covenant is further breached.
Physical betrayal — adultery manifests bodily.
The safest place to stop adultery is before desire becomes consent.

The outward act is frequently the final visible fruit of an inward betrayal already cultivated for some time.
That is why Yeshua addresses the eye and heart before the body.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Theft?

blocks.text: Theft — taking, withholding, using, controlling, or benefiting from what is not rightfully yours.

Stealing is not limited to secretly taking an object. It can include fraud, cheating, exploitation, withheld wages, unpaid debts, dishonest gain, manipulation, plagiarism, taking credit for another's work, misusing another person's time or resources, or obtaining advantage through deceit.
The inward roots are often greed, envy, entitlement, fear of lack, mistrust of YHWH's provision, and the desire to gain by another person's loss.
Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour... that he may have to give to him that needeth.
The deeper question is: Am I receiving rightly, earning honestly, giving freely, and respecting what belongs to another?

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To deal honestly, work faithfully, repay what is owed, respect another person's property and labor, refuse unjust gain, and trust YHWH as Provider rather than seizing what He has not given.
Be content with such things as ye have.
Give to every man that asketh of thee.
Keeping this commandment means moving from taking toward stewardship, labor, fairness, restitution, generosity, and contentment.

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Taking or Withholding What Is Not Yours

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when property, money, labor, access, or resources are taken or withheld unjustly.

examples: Taking money, goods, property, or possessions that belong to another.
Shoplifting, burglary, robbery, embezzlement, or fraud.
Withholding wages, debts, refunds, or payments that are rightfully owed.
Using another person's property without permission.
Keeping something found when the rightful owner can reasonably be identified.
Damaging property and refusing responsibility.
Taking more than one's fair share of shared resources.
Using another person's labor while refusing proper compensation.
dims.keeping: Respect ownership, repay what is owed, return what was wrongly taken, and earn honestly.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Envy, Entitlement, Resentment

blocks.text: The emotional violation begins when another person's possession or prosperity produces resentment or the feeling that one deserves what belongs to them.

examples: Feeling bitter because another has more.
Resenting someone's success so strongly that taking from them feels justified.
Feeling entitled to another person's money, possessions, time, labor, or attention.
Believing another person's abundance somehow wrongs you.
Taking pleasure when someone loses what you envied.
Using emotional manipulation to obtain what was not freely given.
dims.keeping: Practice gratitude, rejoice in another's good, and refuse to let envy become entitlement.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Rationalizing Dishonest Gain

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when the mind constructs reasons why theft is acceptable.

examples: Thinking, They have plenty; they will not miss it.
Thinking, Everyone does it.
Deciding that being underpaid gives permission to steal.
Convincing oneself that digital property, intellectual work, or another's time “does not really count.”
Treating dishonesty as intelligence or cleverness.
Planning how to exploit a loophole without technically being caught.
Believing need automatically creates ownership.

The person who steals uses the life, breath, mind, hands, and opportunity received from YHWH to violate His commandment. Theft therefore does not merely wrong the neighbor; it also dishonors the Giver whose life is being used to take unjustly.

Credit Theft: Taking recognition for another person's labor, ideas, or accomplishments.

Religious Theft: Using God, ministry, fear, promises of blessing, or spiritual authority to obtain money or property dishonestly.
Repentance from theft is not merely feeling sorry while keeping what was taken.
Where reasonably possible, stolen property or unjust gain should be restored.

True repentance seeks to repair what can be repaired.
