commandments.verse: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is False witness?

blocks.text: False witness — presenting something as true when the full testimony of the facts says otherwise.

False witness is broader than consciously inventing a lie. A person may sincerely repeat something false because they did not fully see, did not fully hear, did not investigate, misunderstood what was said, ignored contrary evidence, accepted another person's interpretation, or leaned upon their own understanding.
A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies.
Thus a false witness speaks lies, even when the witness personally believes the statement. Sincerity does not transform false testimony into truth.

The command therefore requires more than “Do not deliberately lie.” It requires the witness to see carefully, hear fully, understand soberly, seek the whole matter, and distinguish fact from interpretation before speaking with certainty.
He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
The deeper question is: Do my words testify to what the evidence actually shows, or merely to what I assumed, inherited, preferred, or was told?

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To love truth above preference; use one's full eyes, full ears, full mind, and full awareness before making judgment; hear the matter completely; distinguish observation from interpretation; examine opposing evidence; and correct one's testimony when facts prove it wrong.
The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.
He that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
A faithful witness must therefore be willing to say: I saw this; I heard this; I believe this; I inferred this; I do not know this. These are not the same statements.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Acting Upon Falsehood, Exposure, and Coordinated Harm

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when false witness, distortion, accusation, malicious exposure, or unverified testimony becomes action that harms another person's privacy, safety, livelihood, freedom, reputation, relationships, or ability to live peacefully.

examples: Filing a knowingly false accusation, complaint, police report, workplace report, or institutional report.
Fabricating, altering, hiding, selectively presenting, or misrepresenting evidence.
Signing testimony one has not personally verified.
Editing screenshots, recordings, photographs, messages, quotations, or documents so others receive a meaning opposite to the complete facts.
Doxing — publishing another person's private identifying information to expose, intimidate, shame, endanger, or invite harassment against them.
Blackmail doxing — threatening to expose an address, identity, family, employment, communications, private history, or other personal information unless the person complies with a demand.

Blackmail or extortion — using true, distorted, fabricated, or private information as leverage to force money, obedience, silence, favors, sexual access, withdrawal of testimony, or some other desired action.
Coordinating others to report someone falsely or deceptively to employers, platforms, authorities, churches, schools, landlords, businesses, or other institutions.
Organized community reporting based upon rumor, ideological hostility, incomplete evidence, or knowingly false claims in order to overwhelm systems and punish a target.
Organizing or encouraging coordinated harassment, stalking, intimidation, mass messaging, unwanted contact, public shaming, or campaigns intended to make another person afraid or socially isolated.
Sending crowds toward someone's home, workplace, family, or online accounts because of an accusation that has not been truthfully established.

Causing another to lose employment, housing, property, freedom, relationships, safety, or reputation through testimony one knows—or should know through reasonable examination—is false or seriously misleading.
Acting against someone merely because many people repeat the same accusation.
Defaming another person's character by spreading damaging claims without sufficient evidence or just cause.

Calling someone a stalker, pervert, pedophile, predator, abuser, thief, liar, criminal, adulterer, murderer, or other morally or socially condemning label without just evidence supporting the accusation.
Repeating such labels publicly, online, at work, in church, within family, or within a community until the repetition itself becomes treated as proof.
Using a severe accusation to trigger reporting systems, social exclusion, investigation, harassment, loss of employment, or public humiliation without adequate factual basis.

after.text: A multitude repeating one unverified story does not transform false testimony into truth.
Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment.

dims.keeping: Establish the matter truthfully before acting. Protect legitimate privacy. Never weaponize another person's private information. Do not join coordinated punishment merely because a crowd, community, platform, leader, or institution claims the accusation is true.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Letting Feeling Become Evidence

blocks.text: The emotional violation occurs when dislike, fear, anger, jealousy, loyalty, humiliation, resentment, or excitement determines what one is willing to believe.

examples: Wanting an accusation to be true because one dislikes the accused.
Believing negative testimony readily because it confirms resentment.
Repeating scandal because it is emotionally exciting.
Feeling satisfaction when another person's reputation collapses.
Defending a false statement because admitting error would be embarrassing.
Refusing contrary evidence because loyalty to one's group feels more important.
Taking emotional hurt as proof of another person's guilt.
Feeling disappointed when a damaging rumor proves false.
Feeling morally justified in applying a severe label because the person makes one uncomfortable, angry, suspicious, or afraid, even where the facts do not establish the accusation.
dims.keeping: Feel honestly, but do not make emotion a witness to facts it cannot establish.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Incomplete Seeing, Hearing, and Understanding

blocks.text: The mental violation occurs when a conclusion is formed before the whole matter has been heard, seen, examined, and understood.
A person can speak falsely without initially intending deception because they failed to use their full eyes, full ears, full mind, and full awareness.

examples: Hearing part of a conversation and assuming the rest.
Seeing an action without knowing its context.
Remembering only details that support one's conclusion.
Confusing inference with observation.
Treating interpretation as though it were the actual words spoken.
Reading one verse while ignoring surrounding verses that establish its meaning.
Repeating what another person taught without examining whether Scripture actually says it.
Believing an accusation because many people repeat it.
Leaning upon one's own understanding and then speaking that understanding as fact.
Ignoring evidence because it contradicts what one has already decided.
Seeing behavior one finds strange or uncomfortable and immediately assigning labels such as stalker, pervert, pedophile, predator, or criminal without establishing the necessary facts.
Treating suspicion, discomfort, rumor, pattern-recognition, or personal interpretation as proof of another person's guilt.

after.text: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.

dims.keeping: Use the full eyes, ears, mind, context, and available evidence before testifying.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Making the Facts Serve the Desired Outcome
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation occurs when truth becomes secondary to winning, reputation, doctrine, money, status, influence, vindication, political victory, religious authority, personal certainty, control.

examples: Selecting only facts that support one's position.
Misrepresenting an opponent to make one's argument stronger.
Refusing correction because one's reputation depends upon being right.
Distorting Scripture because a doctrine, church, teacher, or institution depends upon a particular conclusion.
Repeating dramatic claims because they attract attention or followers.
Protecting a useful lie because admitting truth would cost influence.
Destroying another's reputation to gain position.
Using accusations strategically to eliminate a rival.
Applying a highly damaging label because it is more effective at discrediting the person than presenting the actual facts.
Escalating language from “I am concerned” to “this person is a predator” because the stronger accusation produces greater social power.
dims.keeping: Let truth determine the conclusion rather than determining the conclusion first and recruiting facts afterward.

dims.name: Vocal
dims.subtitle: Speaking Lies as Testimony
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: The vocal violation occurs whenever the mouth states falsely what another person said, did, meant, believed, intended, or was.

examples: Deliberately lying.
Repeating rumor as established fact.
Misquoting someone.
Removing words from context so their meaning changes.
Saying “They said...” when they did not actually say it.
Calling an inference a fact.
Exaggerating an accusation.
Repeating gossip without knowing whether it is true.
Leaving out essential facts so listeners form a false conclusion.
Repeating false teaching as Scripture without examining the testimony of Scripture itself.
Continuing to repeat a claim after clear evidence has corrected it.
Using words to incite others into harassment, exclusion, punishment, or retaliation based upon unverified claims.
Calling someone a stalker, pervert, pedophile, predator, abuser, thief, liar, criminal, adulterer, murderer, or other condemning name without sufficient evidence and just cause.
Repeating accusations in a way that causes listeners to believe guilt has already been established when it has not.
Using the phrase “everyone knows” or “people are saying” to give rumor the appearance of established testimony.

after.text: By thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.

dims.keeping: Speak exactly enough that the listener receives the truth rather than merely the impression one wishes to create.

dims.name: Intentional
dims.subtitle: Choosing the Preferred Story Over the Facts
dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when evidence challenges one's testimony and the person decides to preserve the testimony anyway.

examples: Knowing one's statement is inaccurate and refusing to correct it.
Concealing evidence that would change the conclusion.
Deliberately quoting only part of someone's statement.
Protecting a doctrine after discovering that the text says something different.
Allowing pride to prevent the words, I was wrong.
Intentionally creating an impression one knows the complete facts would contradict.
Coordinating others to spread a claim one knows is uncertain.
Continuing a reporting or harassment campaign after evidence contradicts the accusation.
Using a false or misleading narrative because it still achieves the desired punishment.
Continuing to call someone a stalker, pervert, pedophile, predator, criminal, or other defamatory label after discovering that the evidence does not justify the accusation.
Knowingly using the worst possible interpretation of someone's behavior because it causes greater social damage.
dims.keeping: When truth corrects you, let your testimony change.

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: Bearing False Witness Concerning God

blocks.text: The gravest form is to testify falsely concerning YHWH, His words, His Son, or what Scripture actually says.
A person may inherit a teaching, hear it repeatedly, assume it is biblical, and eventually testify:
The Bible says...
Yet if the words of Scripture say otherwise, repetition does not make the testimony true.

examples: Attributing words to YHWH that He did not speak.
Saying Yeshua taught something contrary to his recorded words.
Allowing Their Will—tradition, denomination, teacher, creed, institution, or majority opinion—to determine what Scripture must mean.
Reading doctrine into a passage instead of allowing the passage to testify.
Ignoring clear contrary statements because they disturb an inherited belief.
Calling one's interpretation “the Word of God” when the actual words say something different.
Misquoting Scripture to condemn another person.
Using God's Name to strengthen an accusation that the evidence does not support.

after.text: Yeshua himself gives a vital example of allowing his testimony to identify him:
Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?
He also prayed:
And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
Within this testimony, Yeshua identifies the Father as the only true God and himself as the one whom the Father sent and as the Son of God.

Therefore, to testify about Yeshua requires allowing his own words to speak. If someone says, “Jesus said he is the only true God,” while his recorded words instead distinguish the only true God from Jesus Christ whom He sent, that statement does not accurately represent the words being cited.

Likewise, saying simply “Jesus is God” as though those were Yeshua's own recorded words must not be confused with what the passages themselves actually say. A doctrine may be argued from interpretation, but interpretation must not be falsely presented as quotation or direct testimony.
A faithful witness asks: What did Yeshua actually say? What did the Father say? What do the words actually testify? Am I repeating Scripture—or repeating someone's interpretation of Scripture?

sections.title: A False Witness May Believe His Own Testimony

blocks.text: This distinction is essential.
A liar may know the statement is false.
A false witness may believe the statement because the witness did not see fully, hear fully, investigate fully, remember carefully, or understand faithfully.
Yet false testimony still produces a lie.
That is why Scripture repeatedly commands careful hearing:
The simple believeth every word.
He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
The obligation of the witness is therefore not merely sincerity.
It is faithfulness to reality.
Defamation is the destruction or unjust injury of another person's name through false or inadequately supported claims.

A person's reputation is part of how they are known among others. To falsely attach a severe moral or criminal label to someone can damage employment, friendships, family relationships, housing, safety, standing in the community, and the willingness of others even to hear their side.

Labels such as stalker, pervert, pedophile, predator, abuser, criminal, thief, murderer, adulterer, or fraud carry enormous weight. They should never be used casually, as insults, as exaggerations, or merely because someone behaves in a way another person dislikes.
A righteous witness asks:
What exactly happened?
What evidence establishes the accusation?
What facts would justify this particular label?
Am I describing observed conduct—or assigning a condemning identity beyond what the evidence proves?
There is a difference between saying:
This behavior concerned me.
and saying:
This person is a stalker.
There is a difference between saying:
That statement was inappropriate.
and saying:
This person is a pervert.
There is a difference between reporting actual evidence of sexual wrongdoing and applying the word pedophile merely to destroy someone's reputation.
Where serious misconduct is genuinely evidenced, truthful reporting is not false witness. But where there is not just evidence and cause, severe accusations themselves can become false witness.

sections.title: When Words And Facts Say Opposite Things

blocks.text: False witness becomes especially evident when a person's claim and the available record plainly contradict one another.
If someone says:
He said X.
But the record plainly says:
I said Y.
the witness must yield to the record.
One should not change “Son of God” into another direct quotation, nor change “the only true God... and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent” into words the passage itself does not say.

Interpretation may be discussed, but quotation must remain quotation, inference must remain inference, doctrine must remain doctrine, accusation must remain accusation until established, and evidence must not be altered to fit the preferred conclusion.

sections.title: Gossip, Doxing, Defamation, And Organized False Witness

blocks.text: Saying “Someone told me”, “Everyone knows”, “People are reporting it”, or “I heard he's a predator” does not remove responsibility.
Every repetition makes the speaker another witness carrying the claim forward.

Doxing, coordinated reporting, public shaming, defamation, and community harassment become especially dangerous when accusation begins substituting for evidence. A crowd can multiply the consequences of one false witness without ever improving the truthfulness of the original claim.
A person can be publicly condemned by hundreds of people who all received their information from the same false or incomplete source.
One accusation repeated one thousand times is still one accusation unless independently supported by facts.

Before repeating or acting upon harmful information, ask: Did I witness this? Have I verified it? Is the source reliable? Do I understand the context? Is the information necessary to disclose? Is the label actually established by evidence? Am I protecting someone from real harm, or inviting punishment before the matter has been established?
A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

sections.title: Truth Without Love Can Still Wound Wrongfully

blocks.text: Not every harmful disclosure is false.
A person may reveal something true and still do so maliciously.
Truth can be weaponized through unnecessary exposure, humiliation, blackmail, intimidation, or disclosure of private information that serves no righteous purpose.
The question is therefore not merely:
Is it true?
But also:
Why am I saying it? Why am I exposing it? What am I trying to cause others to do?
Truth should serve righteous judgment, protection, correction, reconciliation, and justice—not cruelty for its own sake.
Yeshua said:
Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
Appearance is partial.
Righteous judgment seeks the whole matter.
Therefore use both eyes, both ears, the whole mind, context, evidence, and prayerful discernment before turning perception into testimony.
The proper progression is:
See fully · hear fully · examine fully · understand carefully · seek YHWH's counsel · then testify truthfully.

sections.title: When You Are Tempted
sections.q: What should you ask when you are tempted?

blocks.text: Ask: Did I actually see this? Did I actually hear it? Do I know the context? Am I repeating fact, interpretation, inference, tradition, suspicion, accusation, or rumor? Have I examined evidence that disagrees with me? Am I willing to be corrected? Do the words themselves actually say what I claim they say? Is the label I am placing on this person truly justified by evidence? Am I about to expose, report, defame, or punish someone before the matter is established?
Remember:
A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies.
And:
He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.

commandments.verse: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's.

sections.title: Its Opposite
sections.q: What is Coveting?

blocks.text: Coveting — desiring another person's life, relationship, possessions, status, position, success, body, opportunities, property, influence, or blessings in a way that produces envy, resentment, dissatisfaction, comparison, or the wish to possess what is not rightly yours.
Coveting is the hidden inward seedbed from which many other commandments may be violated.
A person may covet before they steal.
Covet before they commit adultery.
Covet before they lie.
Covet before they murder.
Covet before they dishonor.

Coveting is therefore not merely noticing that another person has something desirable. The violation begins when admiration becomes possessive desire, comparison, envy, resentment, entitlement, fixation, or dissatisfaction with what YHWH has presently given.
The deeper question is: Can I see another person's blessing without needing to possess it, diminish it, resent it, or make it the measure of my own worth?

sections.title: To Keep It Inwardly
sections.q: How do you keep this commandment?

blocks.text: To receive one's own life with gratitude; rejoice in another person's good; trust YHWH's provision; seek what is righteous rather than what belongs to another; refuse envy and comparison; and desire blessing without requiring another person's loss.
Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have.
A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

Contentment does not forbid growth, work, improvement, ambition, or prayer for greater provision. It means that desire remains under righteousness rather than becoming hunger for another person's portion.

sections.title: To Violate It Inwardly — The Seven Dimensions
sections.q: How is this commandment broken inwardly?

dims.name: Physical
dims.subtitle: Acting Out Covetous Desire

blocks.text: The physical violation occurs when inward craving produces outward behavior designed to possess, imitate, intrude upon, or take what belongs to another.

examples: Taking another person's property because one has become fixated upon having it.
Pursuing another person's spouse.
Copying another person's life, identity, work, or possessions compulsively out of envy.
Manipulating circumstances to take another person's job, home, inheritance, status, or opportunity.
Spending recklessly to imitate another person's lifestyle.
Intruding repeatedly into another person's relationship, family, private life, or possessions because desire has become obsessive.
Damaging another person's possessions or opportunities because one resents that they have them.
dims.keeping: Respect what belongs to another and let admiration remain admiration without turning into possession.

dims.name: Emotional
dims.subtitle: Envy, Jealousy, Resentment

blocks.text: The emotional violation occurs when another person's good produces bitterness rather than joy.

examples: Feeling resentful because another person is wealthier, more attractive, more loved, more successful, or more influential.
Feeling jealous of another person's marriage or family.
Becoming angry when someone else receives recognition.
Feeling diminished because another person prospers.
Secretly wishing another would lose what they have.
Feeling satisfaction when someone one envies experiences failure.
Comparing constantly until gratitude disappears.

after.text: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?

dims.keeping: Rejoice in another person's blessing without interpreting it as evidence of your own lack.

dims.name: Mental
dims.subtitle: Comparison and Possessive Imagination

blocks.text: The mental violation begins when the mind repeatedly compares, imagines possession, or constructs dissatisfaction.

examples: Thinking continually, Why do they have that and I do not?
Imagining oneself in another person's marriage, house, position, body, career, or life.
Mentally rehearsing how much better life would be if one had what belongs to another.
Measuring one's worth by another person's possessions or success.
Assuming another person's blessing means YHWH has neglected you.
Turning admiration into fixation.
Thinking another person's life would solve one's own inward dissatisfaction.

after.text: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.

dims.keeping: Notice comparison early and return the mind to gratitude, wisdom, and what YHWH actually calls you to pursue.

dims.name: Ambitional
dims.subtitle: Wanting Another Person's Portion
dims.q: How is it broken in ambition?

blocks.text: The ambitional violation occurs when aspiration ceases to be growth toward one's own righteous calling and becomes desire to possess another person's particular portion.

examples: Wanting another person's marriage rather than seeking righteousness in one's own relationships.
Wanting another person's career position specifically because they have it.
Wanting their wealth, influence, audience, title, house, land, status, recognition, or reputation.
Desiring to replace another rather than develop faithfully.
Pursuing success primarily to surpass someone one envies.
Treating another person's life as the blueprint one must possess.
Wanting what they have more than seeking what YHWH wills for you.

after.text: Yeshua said:
Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness.

dims.keeping: Pursue what YHWH has for you without requiring another person's portion to become yours.

dims.subtitle: Speaking From Envy
dims.q: How is it broken in speech?

blocks.text: The vocal violation occurs when coveting begins leaking through speech.

examples: Belittling another person's success because one envies it.

Complaining continually because someone else has more.

dims.keeping: Let speech bless rather than diminish another person's good.

dims.q: How is it broken in the will?

blocks.text: The intentional violation occurs when coveting becomes will.

Attempting to cause another person's failure because their success provokes envy.
Intending to obtain through manipulation what cannot righteously be obtained.
Choosing another person's loss as the path to one's own gain.
dims.keeping: Desire good without consenting to another person's unjust deprivation.

dims.name: Spiritual
dims.subtitle: Dissatisfaction With YHWH's Portion

blocks.text: The deepest form of coveting is not merely wanting another person's possession. It is silently judging that YHWH's present provision, timing, calling, or portion is insufficient.
Coveting can therefore become mistrust.

examples: Believing another person's blessing proves YHWH has treated you unfairly.
Allowing My Will to say, I must have what they have.
Allowing the World's Will to define worth through wealth, beauty, romance, fame, possessions, influence, or status.
Allowing Their Will to pressure you into wanting a life that was never your calling.
Refusing gratitude because your life does not resemble someone else's.
Seeking another person's portion instead of seeking YHWH's counsel for your own.
Desiring the gift more than the Giver.

after.text: Yeshua warns:
Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

dims.keeping: Let YHWH define what life is worth and what portion is righteous for you.

blocks.text: The Tenth Commandment exposes sin before outward action begins.
A person may have stolen nothing.
Touched no one.
Spoken no lie.
Committed no outward act.
Yet inwardly the heart may already be saying:
I want what is theirs.
I resent that they have it.
I should have their life.
I deserve their place.
I would be happier if I possessed their portion.
That is why coveting reaches deeply into the heart.
The progression may be:
seeing · comparison · desire · fixation · envy · resentment · entitlement · intention · action.
The commandment stops the corruption at the beginning.
It is not wrong to see something good and recognize it as desirable.
You may admire another person's marriage and seek to build a healthy marriage.
You may admire someone's discipline and become more disciplined.
You may admire a home and work toward one of your own.
You may admire someone's wisdom, business, craft, strength, faithfulness, or success and learn from them.
The distinction is:
Admiration says: “That is good; I can learn.”
Coveting says: “I want theirs.”
Admiration can inspire righteous growth.
Coveting makes another person's possession the object of inward possession.
Contentment does not mean abandoning ambition, refusing growth, or remaining in harmful circumstances.
Scripture does not command passivity.
Contentment means:
I can pursue better without despising what I have.
I can grow without envying another.
I can ask without demanding another person's portion.
I can build without needing someone else to lose.
The righteous ambition is not:
Give me what belongs to them.
It is:
Father, show me what Thou wouldst have me become, build, receive, and steward.

sections.title: Coveting Can Lead Into The Other Commandments

blocks.text: Coveting another person's possessions can lead to stealing.
Coveting another person's spouse can lead to adultery.
Coveting another person's position can lead to false witness.
Coveting another person's life or inheritance can lead toward murder.
Coveting status and recognition can make self into a god.
Coveting can even make a person resent YHWH Himself because another has received what they desire.
The Tenth Commandment therefore guards the inner doorway before many outward violations occur.

Can I genuinely rejoice if they continue to prosper?
Remember:

stages.subtitle: Wanting Another Person's Portion
warningSigns: Wanting another person's marriage rather than seeking righteousness in one's own relationships.
Wanting another person's career position specifically because they have it.
Wanting their wealth, influence, audience, title, house, land, status, recognition, or reputation.
stages.catch: What desire or ambition did I begin to pursue above obedience?
stages.confess: Name it plainly before YHWH, without excuse.
stages.turn: Lay the ambition down beneath the Kingdom of YHWH.
stages.seek: Ask the Father what is true and right here.
stages.walk: Pursue what YHWH has for you without requiring another person's portion to become yours.

stages.subtitle: Speaking From Envy
warningSigns: Belittling another person's success because one envies it.
Gossiping about someone whose life or possessions provoke jealousy.
Saying their blessing is undeserved without just cause.
stages.catch: What did I say, or agree to say, that pledged me to the wrong thing?
stages.confess: Name it plainly before YHWH, without excuse.
stages.turn: Retract the words; let speech return under the Father.
stages.seek: Ask the Father what is true and right here.
stages.walk: Let speech bless rather than diminish another person's good.

stages.subtitle: Planning to Possess What Belongs to Another
warningSigns: Planning how to take another person's spouse, property, position, inheritance, business, or opportunity.
Deliberately creating circumstances designed to displace another.
Waiting for a marriage to fail so one can pursue the spouse.
stages.catch: What did I decide or consent to, knowing it was against YHWH?
stages.confess: Name it plainly before YHWH, without excuse.
stages.turn: Withdraw consent; choose His will over your own.
stages.seek: Ask the Father what is true and right here.
stages.walk: Desire good without consenting to another person's unjust deprivation.

stages.subtitle: Dissatisfaction With YHWH's Portion
warningSigns: Believing another person's blessing proves YHWH has treated you unfairly.
Allowing My Will to say, I must have what they have.
Allowing the World's Will to define worth through wealth, beauty, romance, fame, possessions, influence, or status.
stages.catch: Whose counsel did I let govern me instead of the Father's?
stages.confess: Name it plainly before YHWH, without excuse.
stages.turn: Renounce the rival counsel and seek the Father alone.
stages.seek: Ask the Father what is true and right here.
stages.walk: Let YHWH define what life is worth and what portion is righteous for you.
